question: Two teams are in a best-two-out-of-three playoff: the teams will play at most \(3\) games, and the winner of the playoff is the first team to win \(2\) games. The first game is played on Team A’s home field, and the remaining games are played on Team B’s home field. Team A has a \(\tfrac23\) chance of winning at home, and its probability of winning when playing away from home is \(p.\) Outcomes of the games are independent. The probability that Team A wins the playoff is \(\tfrac12.\) Then \(p\) can be written in the form \(\tfrac12\!\left(m - \sqrt{n}\right),\) where \(m\) and \(n\) are positive integers. What is \(m + n?\)
solution:
List the possible winning sequences, remembering that the playoff stops as soon as a team earns its second win. Let \(W\) mean a Team A win and \(L\) a Team A loss.

Team A can win in two games only through \(WW\). To win in three games, it must split the first two games and then win the third, giving \(WLW\) or \(LWW\). These three cases are disjoint and include every way Team A can win.

The first-game loss probability is \(1/3\), and an away-game loss has probability \(1-p\). By independence:

| Winning sequence | Probability |
| --- | --- |
| \(WW\) | \(\frac23p\) |
| \(WLW\) | \(\frac23(1-p)p\) |
| \(LWW\) | \(\frac13p^2\) |

Adding these probabilities and setting the result equal to \(1/2\) gives
\[
\frac23p+\frac23(1-p)p+\frac13p^2
=\frac43p-\frac13p^2
=\frac12.
\]
Multiplying by \(6\) and rearranging yields
\[
2p^2-8p+3=0.
\]
The quadratic formula gives
\[
p=\frac{8\pm\sqrt{64-24}}{4}
=\frac{4\pm\sqrt{10}}{2}.
\]
The plus sign produces a value greater than \(1\), so it cannot be a probability. Therefore
\[
p=\frac12(4-\sqrt{10}).
\]
Thus \(m=4\), \(n=10\), and \(m+n=\boxed{14}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
